messages:
anya: Heads-up: preview dashboard showing an unexpected *drop* in dedupe rate and a correlated small dip in invoice-preview for many tenants on shard-4 at 07:45 UTC. Not a spike this time, more like missing duplicates.
mike: Huh. so dedupe rate dropped (fewer dups detected) and preview tokens went down? Could be a fingerprint entropy regression.
devops-bot: deploy 1767755554 to ingest-serializer completed at 07:43 UTC (user: mike).
anya: That timing fits. If serializer changed canonicalization, fingerprints could be more stable and collapse slightly different requests into one, or conversely, lower-entropy fingerprints could *miss* duplicates if hash truncated. We need to confirm.
tasha: grabbing sample pairs from ingress logs around 07:44. Quick grep:
```
grep "fp=" /var/log/ingest/ingest-logs-07-44.log | head -n 50
```
Shows many fingerprints ending with same suffix but different prefixes. Looks like we switched to a new murmur3 variant that truncated to 48 bits.
mike: oh crap, my perf patch swapped in a smaller hash for speed and I forgot the truncation config. I thought dedupe consumer would use fingerprint+request_id, but it actually relies solely on fingerprint for preview dedupe (legacy).
anya: that's the problem then: lower-bit fingerprint increases collision probability which reduces observed duplicates (two events with same request become different fingerprints), causing preview to *under-count* duplicates and thus underreport token usage. That explains the dip.
billing: under-reporting is bad — customers see lower previews; we need to ensure we don't underbill accidentally once fixed. What's the window affected?
sam: quick export shows ~2k requests in the 07:40-07:50 window on shard-4 where fingerprint entropy changed. Tenant list small (~50 tenants). I'll upload CSV to ENGPLAT-9344.
mike: immediate mitigation: revert serializer to previous hash implementation and re-roll at canary only after we update dedupe consumer to include (request_id,fingerprint) as fallback. Rolling back now.
devops-bot: rollback 1767755554 initiated by mike at 07:47 UTC.
tasha: recommend also running a reconciliation job: re-hash original payloads with the old fingerprint function for the window and re-run dedupe on preview to recompute deltas. Sam, can you schedule?
sam: scheduling one-shot job: will run rehash+dige on 07:55 and produce candidate corrections. Will tag billing for dry-run results.
billing: please provide dry-run CSV before we apply anything. We'll not auto-apply until signoff; manual credits may be needed if preview diff >0.3% for any tenant.
anya: long-term: update the metering contract to always include stable request_id in clientlib and make preview dedupe key composite (request_id or fingerprint) to tolerate hash changes. Also add a canary gate in serializer deploys to ensure fingerprint entropy metrics are stable.
mike: agreed. i'll open a PR to restore full-entropy murmur3 and add a deployment test measuring "fingerprint_entropy_entropy" metric (lol) and a canary threshold.
tasha: also adding dashboard card: "fingerprint_collision_rate by shard" + alert if collision_rate > 0.05% over 5m.
anya: created ENGPLAT-9344 to track rollback, rehash job, and RFC for composite dedupe key. Assigning to mike+sam+tasha. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGPLAT-9344
mike: rolling back now and will post logs in the ticket. Sorry everyone.
sam: will post dry-run in ENGPLAT-9344 once job finishes.
anya: thanks — keep thread updates brief and paste tenant export to the ticket. :thumbsup:
